A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSF/METRA research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original representation analyses, skill-learning benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity studies, and failed MiniHack experiments in Section 6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark learning curves, representation measurements, ablations, and the MiniHack failure report.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same representation objective, intrinsic reward, successor-feature critic, and policy updates. Correcting the policy symbol in the algorithm summary aligns the prose with the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Ant, HalfCheetah, Quadruped, Humanoid, Kitchen, and Robobin, with the same goal-reaching and hierarchical-control tasks. Appendix C.6 retains the same MiniHack-Corridor-R5-v0 experiment.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain METRA, CIC, DIAYN, DADS, and VISR, with unchanged experiment-specific subsets. For example, Figure 6 retains METRA, DIAYN, and VISR as the goal-reaching comparators.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model and skill dimensions, goal sampling, evaluation metrics, and hierarchical-controller procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 50-goal evaluation, staying-time-fraction metric, and settings in Tables 1–3.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the same representation checks, contrastive-loss and information-bottleneck ablations, critic-parameterization tests, hyperparameter sensitivities, trajectory visualizations, and MiniHack failure analysis.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations across ten seeds for the main comparisons, five seeds for Appendix C.3, and two for C.4. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: The result curves, numerical measurements, and qualitative findings are retained. Examples include the 0.9884 empirical representation-distance average in Section 6.1 and the 0.2309 regression slope in Appendix C.1; the task-specific CSF–METRA comparisons also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Corollary 1 now states that METRA approximates the contrastive lower bound on mutual information, whereas v2 said it approximates mutual information itself. This corrects the formal assertion to match its existing displayed relation; the supporting derivations and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explaining METRA through MISL, deriving the simpler CSF algorithm with comparable performance, and identifying important information-bottleneck and parameterization ingredients.

C2.justification: The exploration and representation interpretations remain substantively unchanged. Both retain the scaling and offline-pretraining limitations in Section 7 and the proposed explanations for MiniHack failures in Appendix C.6.

D1.justification: Both retain the same architecture and hyperparameter tables, hardware and runtime disclosures, and code and website access information. The added explanation of parameter symbols in Section 5.2 clarifies existing notation without adding implementation settings.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the distinctions from METRA, CIC, and VISR and connections to contrastive learning and successor features.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar, punctuation, and terminology edits throughout the main text and appendices, corrects the policy notation, explains parameter symbols, and expands the wording of the Appendix C.4 heading. The section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 reformats the author block, colors citations and cross-references, and makes modest spacing and placement changes, including moving Corollary 1 onto the preceding page. All figures and tables are retained with unchanged data displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by correcting Corollary 1's claim about what is approximated and aligning the policy notation with Algorithm 1. Copyediting also improves readability. These are limited gains because the method, supporting derivations, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
